newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Greens reject alliance with ex-communists.
newsitem.headline: German Greens reject alliance with ex-communists.

text.p: Germany's Greens said on Friday they wanted to govern with the main opposition Social Democrats after elections in 1998 and ruled out a coalition with the ex-communist Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS).

"We rule out cooperation with the Party of Democratic Socialism, either in a coalition or by establishing a minority government tolerated by the PDS," the Greens said in a statement after a meeting in the east German town of Woerlitz.
The statement followed the defection of two east German members in protest at what they saw as a softening of the party's opposition to the PDS.

The two defectors were among seven former civil rights activists who joined Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU), saying it provided the best guarantee that the East German communists they once fought would not get back into power.
The news caused a sensation in eastern Germany, where the activists were well known for helping to found democratic parties in the dying days of communist East Germany.

The Greens face a particular dilemma in the east, where most of their members came from the anti-communist civil rights movement and where the party's environmental concerns rank low in ordinary citizens' priorities.

For this reason some Greens, like many Social Democrats in east Germany, have openly toyed with the idea of forming an alliance with the PDS, the third party in east Germany, which could potentially hold the balance of power in Bonn after 1998.
